Radiology Report
Date: 08/27/2026
Patient: Alison Homenick, 66-year-old female

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/27/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Focal kyphotic deformity at T11 measuring 24 degrees.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture involving the T11 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. Additionally, a focal kyphotic deformity is noted at T11 measuring 24 degrees.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on these imaging findings.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/04/2026
Patient: Alison Homenick, 66-year-old female

History of Present Illness:
Back pain began 07/25/2026 after a fall from standing height, 6 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 5 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and calcitonin nasal spray, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Clinical Course:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 21/24.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current conservative management and monitor symptoms closely. Consider further intervention if pain worsens or functional status declines.
